item.title: Nvidia Launches Next-Gen AI Chips, Rubin Platform Enters Production
item.description: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang announced the company's next generation of chips is in "full production," designed to deliver five times the artificial-intelligence computing power of previous chips for chatbots and other AI applications. These chips are expected to debut later this year.

item.title: Dell Revives XPS Laptop Brand for Premium Market Push
item.description: Dell has reintroduced its XPS laptop lineup, a year after retiring the premium brand, in an effort to boost demand within a challenging personal computer market. This move represents a U-turn for the company, following "very broad" feedback from its partners.

item.title: Lego Unveils Smart Brick, Integrating Advanced Technology into Play
item.description: Lego unveiled its technology-packed Smart Brick at CES 2026, introducing a new era of connected play. This standard-sized 2 x 4 brick features a speaker, LED lights, and a tiny chip, enabling sets to respond to user interaction and construction.

item.title: Hyundai, Boston Dynamics Unveil Atlas Humanoid Robot at CES
item.description: Hyundai-owned Boston Dynamics publicly demonstrated its humanoid robot Atlas for the first time at the CES tech showcase, intensifying competition with Tesla and other organisations developing human-like robots. The unveiling highlights efforts to build machines that resemble and perform tasks like people.

item.title: Meta Pauses Ray-Ban Display Glasses Global Launch Amid Strong US Demand
item.description: Meta has delayed the international expansion of its Ray-Ban Display glasses, citing strong demand in the United States and a constrained supply. The company will prioritise fulfilling US orders while re-evaluating its approach to international availability.

item.title: Singapore, Beijing Rank Among Top Global Tech Cities in Savills Matcha Index
item.description: Singapore and Beijing have emerged as two of the world’s most liveable cities for technology workers, according to Savills’ inaugural Matcha Index. The index evaluates locations based on their "buzz" and the quality of spaces where employees can collaborate and socialise.

item.title: Vietnam to Limit Online Ad Skip Time to Five Seconds
item.description: Vietnam’s new regulation will require online video and moving image advertisements to allow users to skip them within five seconds, effective Feb. 15, 2026. This decree prohibits digital service providers from forcing viewers to watch unskippable ads longer than five seconds.

item.title: Spotify Expands Creator Monetisation, Opens Los Angeles Studio
item.description: Spotify is expanding its monetisation program for creators and introducing new tools for video podcasters. The move aims to enhance competition with platforms such as YouTube and Netflix in the growing market.

item.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Health for Integrated Medical Records, Wellness Apps
item.description: OpenAI on Wednesday launched a new ChatGPT Health tab, allowing users to connect medical records and wellness applications, such as Apple Health and MyFitnessPal. The feature aims to answer health-related questions directly within the chatbot.

item.title: Razer Unveils Project Ava AI Gaming Assistant’s Physical Form
item.description: Razer has unveiled a new physical hardware device for Project Ava, its real-time AI gaming co-pilot, at CES 2026. This new version aims to make the AI assistant feel more physically present for gamers.
